statement: For 2D rectangular knapsack with 8-12 item types, co-evolving per-type placement method assignments (BSSF/BAF/BL/CP/BLSF) alongside type ordering improves packing profit by ~0.4 points over uniform-method search, because different item geometries benefit from different placement heuristics.
regime: Bins 900-2000, 8-12 item types with diverse geometries, 5 placement methods, 1s time budget
mechanism: Items with high aspect ratios benefit from BL (bottom-left) placement which creates regular stacking; compact items benefit from BSSF (best short-side fit) which minimizes waste; items near bin edges benefit from CP (contact-point) which reduces interior fragmentation. The 5^M method space (390K-244M configurations) contains many local optima that a co-evolutionary search with elite pool, crossover, and mutation can efficiently explore.
applicability_bounds: Requires multiple item types with diverse geometries. With only 1-2 types, all methods produce similar results. Benefit diminishes with >5 methods (search space grows faster than improvement).

statement: Gap-fill post-processing (adding items by density to remaining free rects after the main greedy pass) is safe and adds ~0.02 points ONLY when applied to the single best solution at the end. Applying gap-fill to every packing call causes TLE and drops score by ~6 points.
regime: 1s time budget, 15 test cases, hundreds of packing evaluations in random search
mechanism: Each gap-fill pass scans all types against all free rects (O(M × free_rects)), which adds ~50-100ms per packing. With hundreds of random search iterations, this overhead compounds to exceed the 1s time limit on large test cases. Limiting gap-fill to the final best solution avoids the compounding.
applicability_bounds: Specific to tight time budgets (<1s) with many packing evaluations. With longer time budgets, gap-fill per iteration might be affordable.
